entry.title: Using BBR on an Android device
entry.content:
Enabling BBR on Redmi K80 via a Kernel Module

Device: Redmi K80 (zorn / 24117RK2CC)
System: HyperOS OS3.0.309.0.WOKCNXM / Android 16
Kernel: 6.1.138-android14-11-g965475777129-mi
Root: SukiSU Ultra 4.3.0 (LKM mode)

Result: BBR and fq are now up and running on this device, persisting across reboots. No kernel flashing, no waiting for Xiaomi to release the kernel source, and none of the screen flickering issues seen with GKI.

This post documents the entire process: how to confirm BBR is missing from the kernel, why a standard insmod fails, how to track down the matching source tree and compiler, how to avoid instant reboots upon loading, and finally how to package it into an auto-starting KernelSU module.

First, What Is BBR?

BBR is a TCP congestion control algorithm introduced by Google in 2016. Traditional algorithms like cubic rely on packet loss to detect congestion: the moment packets start dropping, cubic drastically cuts its sending rate. BBR takes a different approach—it estimates the bottleneck bandwidth and round-trip propagation time of the link, then paces packet transmission according to that model.

This difference is most noticeable on weak, high-latency links with some random packet loss. BBR generally keeps sender throughput higher while keeping queues short, preventing latency from piling up. That said, it is not a “speed hack”: peak bandwidth won’t magically increase out of thin air, and download speeds depend largely on the server’s congestion control algorithm and the link itself.

Android kernels don’t always ship with BBR compiled in. Many OEM configurations only keep reno and cubic to save build size and reduce behavioral variables. That is exactly the case on this K80.

Checking Kernel Support

First, check the currently available congestion control algorithms:

Next, check the kernel configuration:

CONFIG_TCP_CONG_ADVANCED is not enabled, so BBR was never compiled at all. There is no tcp_bbr.ko under /vendor/lib/modules, and no bbr symbols in the kernel symbol table either.

In other words, it’s not a matter of a toggle being left off—the algorithm simply isn’t in the kernel.

Why Not Just Build a Full Kernel?

The standard approach would be to compile a full kernel with BBR enabled and flash it to the boot partition. There are two problems with that here.

First, Xiaomi hasn’t released the source code for 6.1.138-mi. MiCode only has the older bsp-zorn-v-oss (6.1.68 / Android 15), with no branch corresponding to Android 16.

Second, flashing a generic GKI or third-party kernel breaks the HyperOS display stack. I tested both a generic GKI 6.1.145 and a third-party zorn 6.1.176 kernel on this phone; both booted, but the screen flickered constantly while the vendor HWC/DRM repeatedly spammed COMMIT failed: 11. At the time, it looked like the vendor display modules were tightly coupled to the exact kernel version, meaning any kernel swap would break the display.

2026-11-05 Correction: That assessment was only half right. The flickering wasn’t because “newer kernels are inherently incompatible,” but rather because a DRM validation check introduced in stable 6.1.141 conflicted with possible_clones in zorn’s vendor msm_drm. Reverting that check fixed the display on 6.1.176. See “6.1.176: Display Compatibility and Dual BBR” at the end of this post for details.

So while building a full kernel seemed like a dead end at the time, it later proved to be fixable rather than impossible.

The Third Way: Loading a Module at Runtime

Even without replacing the full kernel, the stock kernel itself supports loadable modules. If we can compile a tcp_bbr.ko and load it at runtime, we don’t need to touch the boot partition or risk disturbing the display stack.

The catch is that standard insmod will reject the module.

There are three checks between a module and the kernel:

  1. vermagic: The kernel version string embedded in the module at build time must match the running kernel;
  2. MODVERSIONS: If the kernel has CONFIG_MODVERSIONS enabled, every external symbol referenced by the module carries a CRC checksum that the kernel verifies one by one;
  3. Symbol export: Symbols referenced by the module must exist in the kernel’s export table.

This phone’s kernel has CONFIG_MODVERSIONS=y, and the OEM didn’t provide Module.symvers, so a self-compiled module won’t have matching CRCs. Its vermagic will also mismatch because it lacks the -mi suffix.

A direct insmod will fail at the first or second check.

What ksud insmod Does

ksud insmod in SukiSU 4.3.0 doesn’t just blindly call init_module. It includes a userspace module loader that roughly does the following:

  1. Reads the .ko and parses undefined symbols in the ELF;
  2. Resolves the address of each symbol via the kernel symbol query interface (UAPI 6) or /proc/kallsyms;
  3. Rewrites the symbol table entries to SHN_ABS with their values set to the real addresses;
  4. Calls init_module;
  5. If the kernel rejects the module due to a vermagic mismatch, reads the expected vermagic from the kernel log, patches the string inside the .ko, and retries.

Once the symbols are rewritten as absolute addresses, the kernel no longer checks the export table or CRCs during module loading, and the vermagic is patched to match the device’s actual string. That’s how it manages to load “foreign” .ko files.

vpnhide_kmod.ko on the phone is a ready-made example. Its vermagic says 6.1.166-dirty, yet it loads and works fine on this 6.1.138-mi kernel.

Keep in mind, however, that ksud insmod only bypasses symbol and version checks. If struct layouts or CFI hashes don’t match, the module will still crash the kernel—often causing an instant reboot upon loading before any logs can be saved.

Hurdle 1: The Source Must Be ACK

My first build of the module used upstream stable 6.1.138 from kernel.org. It compiled cleanly, but when I compared the device BTF against the module BTF, every single struct size was off:

StructDevice BTFstable 6.1.138Diff
sock85676888
inet_sock1088984104
inet_connection_sock15361392144
tcp_sock23682200168
module1088102464

The kernel version string is 6.1.138-android14-11-g965475777129-mi. There is more information packed in here than just “6.1.138”:

  • 6.1.138 is the upstream stable version;
  • -android14-11 indicates the android14-6.1 branch of the Android Common Kernel (ACK);
  • -g965475777129 is the commit hash of the build tree;
  • -mi represents Xiaomi’s own patches.

ACK is not mainline. It includes Android-specific patches and adds extra fields to kernel structs:

  • android_kabi_reserved*, controlled by CONFIG_ANDROID_KABI_RESERVE;
  • android_oem_data1, controlled by CONFIG_ANDROID_VENDOR_OEM_DATA;
  • Backported ACK fields like sk_wait_pending;
  • btf_data_size / btf_data inside struct module.

tcp_sock was shifted by a full 168 bytes. When BBR tried to read snd_cwnd, delivered, or app_limited, it would hit completely wrong memory offsets. A bug like this might not crash immediately, waiting instead to trigger on a retransmission or RTT sample.

So the source tree had to be switched to an official ACK tag. I used the GKI release tag from the TUNA mirror:

Verify the version:

The g965475777129 hash in uname -r is from Xiaomi’s internal build tree and does not exist in the public ACK repository. Searching public repos for that hash won’t turn up anything.

Hurdle 2: Matching the Compiler to the Kernel

The device configuration contains this line:

And the kernel also enables:

BBR’s function pointers are called indirectly by the kernel through struct tcp_congestion_ops. At indirect call sites, kCFI checks the type hash at the target function’s entry point. Because CFI_PERMISSIVE is not set, a hash mismatch causes an immediate kernel panic.

This means you can’t just pick any random compiler. It’s best to use the exact same AOSP clang r487747c (17.0.2) that built the kernel.

You can do a sparse checkout from TUNA’s platform/prebuilts/clang/host/linux-x86 repository:

This directory is about 2.3GB.

I also compared the kCFI hashes generated by clang 17.0.2 and 18.1.3 for the function prototypes in tcp_congestion_ops, and they turned out identical. Still, IR and ABI details can vary across compiler versions, so stick to the exact kernel compiler version whenever possible.

Hurdle 3: struct module Missing 16 Bytes

This was the trickiest part of the whole process, and the real culprit behind the “instant reboot upon loading.”

To avoid needing a locally built vmlinux for BTF encoding, I initially disabled these two options:

The module compiled fine, and ksud insmod made it to the loading stage—whereupon the phone instantly rebooted. /sys/fs/pstore was empty, /proc/last_kmsg didn’t exist, and dmesg retained nothing from the previous boot.

With no logs, I had to look at the ABI. Pulling the device BTF and module BTF for a field-by-field comparison revealed:

The device had two extra 8-byte fields:

These are guarded by CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF_MODULES. Because the module was missing those 16 bytes, the kernel read the module’s .gnu.linkonce.this_module section using its own struct module layout. mod->init ended up pointing to a bogus address; the kernel jumped to an invalid pointer, and the phone rebooted.

The fix isn’t simply turning BTF back on. If you turn it on, the module build tries to generate BTF, which in turn requires compiling a full local vmlinux with BTF—a massive undertaking.

The actual trick is to keep the macros enabled during C compilation while skipping the BTF encoding step in make:

This way, both macros remain defined in include/generated/autoconf.h, so the C code sees the exact right struct module layout, while passing empty variables on the make command line skips the BTF generation step.

Check the section size in the compiled module:

This is quite counterintuitive: for the module to load, you must not disable the BTF config options. The config header dictates struct layout, whereas the build rules dictate whether BTF data is actually generated—the two have to be handled separately.

Other Build Pitfalls

Aside from the three major hurdles above, I ran into a few smaller snags during the build.

TRIM_UNUSED_KSYMS

The device config contains:

The source tree doesn’t have abi_symbollist.raw, causing make prepare to fail immediately with:

The fix is to disable symbol trimming:

This has no effect on the module’s ABI.

Missing asm-offsets.h

modules_prepare doesn’t always generate include/generated/asm-offsets.h. Without it, compilation fails with:

Generate it manually:

Missing scripts/module.lds

Linking the module may fail with:

Generate it with:

Module Compression

CONFIG_MODULE_COMPRESS_* produces .ko.zst or .ko.xz files, whereas ksud insmod expects a raw .ko. I disabled compression in the build script.

modpost undefined Warnings

Without Module.symvers, modpost will spit out a bunch of warnings like:

This is normal. Those symbols will be resolved at load time by ksud insmod via kallsyms and don’t need to be resolved at build time.

Verifying the ABI with BTF

Just because a module loads doesn’t mean its ABI is valid. A much more reliable check is comparing the device BTF against the module BTF.

  1. Pull /sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux from the phone;
  2. Generate BTF from the module’s DWARF info using pahole --btf_encode_detached;
  3. Dump both sides using bpftool btf dump ... format raw;
  4. Compare them field by field.

All key structs must match completely in the end:

StructDeviceModule
tcp_sock23682368
tcp_congestion_ops192192
rate_sample7272
sock856856
inet_sock10881088
inet_connection_sock15361536
module10881088

If you see any only-in-device, only-in-module, or MISMATCH, do not load the module. Double-check your source tree, config, and compiler first—never take “it didn’t crash when loaded” as proof that the ABI is right.

scripts/verify-layouts.py in the repository automates this check.

Loading the Module and Setting Up qdisc

Load the module:

Confirm that the module registered successfully:

The OEM default qdisc is mq + pfifo_fast. While BBR has internal pacing, it works best when paired with fq:

On multi-queue devices, setting net.core.default_qdisc=fq won’t override the mq default, so you have to replace the qdisc on each interface individually.

Replacing it doesn’t flatten the hardware queues into a single queue. In Linux 6.1, qdisc_restart() still uses skb_get_tx_queue(dev, skb) to select the hardware queue based on queue_mapping. What changes is the software scheduling layer: multiple TX queues now share a single fq instance, and enqueue/dequeue operations across all queues contend on the same qdisc lock.

On a phone, this trade-off is completely fine. Wi-Fi and cellular speeds are nowhere near high enough for a single qdisc lock to become a bottleneck, whereas fq’s pacing and per-flow queuing are much more beneficial to BBR.

Finally, I packaged everything into a KernelSU module:

  • post-fs-data.sh: loads the .ko as early as possible;
  • service.sh: sets bbr and fq;
  • Background watchdog: checks the qdisc every 30 seconds to prevent netd from resetting fq back to pfifo_fast during network switches.

Verified across reboots: the default CC is bbr, relevant interfaces use fq as their qdisc, and the watchdog runs cleanly under init.

Real-World Performance of This Setup

BBR primarily improves queuing latency under load rather than consistently boosting peak throughput. The noticeable difference in daily use comes from responsiveness, not speedtest numbers.

If your goal is “faster downloads,” changing congestion control on the phone usually yields very little benefit because the download direction is governed by the server. BBR’s impact is much more direct when the phone is the sender—such as uploads, proxy tunnels, and mobile hotspot sharing.

Methodology

From the afternoon into the evening of 2026-11-02, I ran A/B comparisons over Zhejiang Unicom 5G, followed by an additional evening peak session from 22:42 to 22:56. The device was the Redmi K80 on kernel 6.1.138 using tcp_bbr.ko (BBRv1) from the repo. Testing took place indoors on campus, with RSRP hovering just above -100 dBm and SINR ranging from -1 to 14 across different rounds.

There were two test arms:

ArmCongestion Controlqdisc
Acubicmq + pfifo_fast (OEM default)
Cbbrfq

Only the phone side was changed; the servers remained untouched. Three speedtest servers were used: netcup Manassas (~290 ms), Alibaba Cloud Japan (~110 ms), and Alibaba Cloud Beijing (default config, untuned, ~70 ms). The server software was iliyian/minimal-speedtest. Each round spun up a fresh curl connection in an alternating ABBA pattern with a 3-second pause between rounds; downloads transferred 32 MB and uploads 8 MB. During testing, the module’s 30-second qdisc watchdog was paused, and each round verified the active qdisc via tc and confirmed via ss that the socket actually used the intended CC.

For downloads, the client only sees received bytes—cwnd and delivery_rate in ss are sender-side metrics and remain static on the phone. Therefore, download evaluation looked only at application-layer throughput, loaded ping, and NIC byte counters.

Downloads

None of the three servers showed a reproducible difference in download speeds:

In the Beijing normal-signal row, the medians of both arms were identical, though the BBR arm had two rounds dip to 8.6 / 10.5 Mbps, with pair-wise differences swinging from -57% to +29% and showing no consistent direction. In the evening peak row, the arm medians differed by just 2.2%, with pair-wise swings from -54% to +236%—again, no consistent trend. The Japan figures exclude one round with a sudden signal drop and another interrupted by an incoming phone call.

Beijing also saw one weak-signal session (SINR 0–6) where the BBR arm’s median download was 26% higher, but pair-wise differences ranged from -52% to +102%. Under those conditions, results are dominated by radio-layer retransmissions and scheduling rather than BBR.

The reason is simple: during downloads, the phone is the receiver, and congestion control lives on the server. Changing the CC on the phone doesn’t change how the server sends packets; it only affects the ACK path. To actually get BBR benefits on downloads, BBR has to be enabled on the server.

Uploads

The upload direction was much more consistent. Here the phone is the sender, so its CC is actively in charge. BBR didn’t win on throughput, but its send queues were dramatically shorter:

The Beijing normal-signal set is the clearest illustration: loaded upload ping p95 dropped from 237 ms to 64 ms, at the cost of ~15% lower throughput. The evening peak set was even more dramatic: with upload speeds constrained to 1–2 Mbps, CUBIC pushed sender RTT to 3.98 s with a 4.09% retransmission rate, whereas BBR kept RTT at 321 ms and retransmissions at 0.99%—trading ~12% throughput for vastly better latency and packet loss. On the Japan server, throughput was basically a tie while BBR shaved 250–480 ms off latency. On netcup, where RTT is high and the path more congested, BBR lost the most throughput, yet still brought RTT down from 866 ms to 670 ms.

This aligns with how BBR works: it paces traffic according to estimated bandwidth instead of filling up buffers, whereas CUBIC grows its window until packet loss occurs, easily bloating deep cellular uplink buffers. On links like this, throughput and latency are a trade-off.

A Packet Loss Incident

During testing, an incoming call rang for 3 seconds before being declined. In that round, BBR’s retransmission rate spiked to 5.32%, transmit overhead hit 7.3%, and throughput dropped from ~7 Mbps to 3.9 Mbps. BBRv1 backs off noticeably when encountering packet loss; under weak signal or link jitter, it won’t necessarily outperform CUBIC.

Conclusion

On this phone, BBR behaves exactly as designed: its job isn’t to inflate peak bandwidth, but to keep queuing delay down.

The most immediate gains are on uploads. Against the default-configured Beijing server, sender RTT dropped from 804 ms to 193 ms and loaded upload ping p95 dropped from 237 ms to 64 ms, while sacrificing only ~15% throughput. During evening peak hours, CUBIC hit 4-second RTTs and 4% retransmissions compared to BBR’s 0.3 seconds and 1%, with only a ~12% throughput difference. Against the Japan server, throughput was essentially tied while shaving 250–480 ms of latency. For video calls, remote desktop, or hotspot sharing, BBR will feel noticeably snappier than CUBIC.

In the download direction, there was neither a reproducible improvement nor a consistent regression. As noted earlier, downloads are dictated by the server’s CC, so enabling BBR on the client shouldn’t be expected to speed them up; server-side configuration is what matters there.

Achieving these latency gains without flashing a custom kernel or wiping the device means this module setup has met its goal. If you care more about peak upload throughput, switching back to CUBIC temporarily is just a single sysctl command away, or you can disable the module to keep CUBIC permanently. If you care about responsiveness and low latency during uploads, BBR is well worth keeping.

These figures apply specifically to BBRv1, this China Unicom link, and these three servers; different networks, servers, or kernel versions may yield different results. Full methodology, round-by-round data, and limitations are available in the repo:

  • Report: docs/bench/2026-11-02-bbr-vs-cubic.md
  • Per-round CSV: docs/bench/data/2026-11-02-runs.csv
  • Per-sample data: ss / ping
  • Repository: https://github.com/iliyian/k80-zorn-bbr

BBRv2 and BBRv3

I also evaluated both newer versions along the way.

BBRv3 cannot be built as a standalone module. It depends on new fields and functions in the core networking stack:

  • struct rate_sample adds tx_in_flight, is_ece, and is_acking_tlp_retrans_seq, which are populated by the core TCP stack;
  • struct tcp_sock adds fast_ack_mode and tlp_orig_data_app_limited;
  • New helper functions like tcp_plb_* and tcp_skb_tx_in_flight_is_suspicious;
  • ICSK_CA_PRIV_SIZE increases from 104 bytes to 144 bytes.

All of these require modifying kernel headers and recompiling the entire kernel, which a loadable module cannot do. Google’s v3 branch is distributed as a full kernel tree for this reason.

2026-11-04 Update: BBRv3 has now been backported to the ACK 6.1.138 kernel and verified on the device.
bbr3 registers and switches cleanly, with boot, audio, and module loading all working normally. For the porting process, core stack patches,
BTF/CRC verification, and troubleshooting notes, see bbrv3/README.md.
The point that “it cannot be built as a module” still stands—this is a full kernel patchset, not a .ko.

BBRv2 is a different story. Compiling tcp_bbr.c from v2alpha-2022-08-28 against ACK 6.1.138 only requires removing the deprecated .tso_segs field; sizeof(struct bbr) is 104 bytes, matching 6.1’s icsk_ca_priv exactly, so BUILD_BUG_ON passes. It only uses fields already present in 6.1 without touching the core stack.

However, v2 is an experimental branch from 2022 that never made it into mainline, and its behavior on mobile networks hasn’t been validated. It would also need to be renamed to bbr2 to coexist with the existing bbr. It’s a viable direction for future tinkering, but I didn’t deploy it this time.

BBRv3 Benchmarks: Latency Gains, No Throughput Gains

Late on 2026-11-04 into the early hours of 11-05, I ran another A/B test on the same K80 with the bbr3 kernel port. This session focused purely on benchmarking without any kernel or patch changes. The network was switched to the default SIM card (China Telecom), which fell back to LTE during testing (download RSRP −87 dBm / SNR 24, upload −94 / SNR 17) rather than the Unicom 5G link from 11-02. The server was still the default-configured Alibaba Cloud Beijing instance.

The test arms matched the previous setup:

Cbbr3fq

Each round launched a fresh curl in an alternating ABBA pattern with a 3-second gap between rounds; 6 pairs of 32 MiB downloads and 4 pairs of 8 MiB uploads were run. The bbr3_fq module’s watchdog was paused during testing, and each round verified the qdisc via tc, confirmed the active socket CC via ss, and checked that routing bypassed tun. The unmodified cc_bench.sh harness was used.

Looking round by round, cubic’s RTT p95 ranged from 1.9 to 4.8 s, while bbr3 stayed at 0.30–0.42 s (excluding the first round); cwnd p95 was 747–1069 segments vs 57–76 segments (234 in the first round). Cubic’s p95 essentially reflects its buffer ceiling, whereas bbr3’s p95 comes from probe cycles nudging cwnd from ~50 up to ~70.

A sample size of 4 pairs is small. Queue metrics achieved 4/4 complete separation: an exact paired sign-flip test gives p=0.125 (the minimum possible for n=4), and a paired t-test gives p=0.0005–0.011 (assuming normality); paired tests for throughput give p=0.81–0.88. An unpaired permutation test would yield p=0.029 for the queue metrics, but given the paired ABBA design, that figure is overly optimistic and shouldn’t be used to draw conclusions.

There is no distinguishable difference between the two in latency or throughput, though v3 is slightly more conservative with cwnd. However, since this compares data across different days, carriers, and kernels, it shouldn’t be treated as a strict v1-vs-v3 A/B test.

Why There Were No Extra Gains

  • The port used a 2025-03 v3 snapshot with PLB and ecn_low stripped out; those paths would have been dead code on this device anyway, leaving behavior very close to v1.
  • v3’s main improvements over v1 revolve around loss recovery, ECN, and PLB. In this test, total TCP retransmissions on both sides were just 69 segments (0.28%), with zero RTOs, zero SYN retransmits, and no ECN—giving those mechanisms nothing to do.
  • The bottleneck was LTE uplink scheduling at just 2–3.5 Mbps. Both versions kept a cwnd more than large enough to saturate the uplink; any excess cwnd simply turns into queuing delay.
  • On a single flow over a clean link, BBR’s fairness and coexistence improvements don’t come into play either.

Measurement Pitfalls

  • The download direction is structurally invalid for client-side CC testing: the phone is the receiver and CC runs on the server, so nothing changed on the phone can improve download throughput.
  • A 4-pair sample requires paired statistical tests; unpaired permutation artificially lowers p to 0.029, whereas an ABBA design must be analyzed in pairs.
  • ping’s icmp_seq starts at 1. Assuming it starts at 0 fabricates 0.5–2.9% phantom packet loss; actual ICMP loss in this session was 0.
  • Cubic’s deep queue drain can pollute the immediately following bbr3 round. The first bbr3 round had a p95 of 1546 ms compared to 300–415 ms in the subsequent three rounds; a 3-second cooldown isn’t enough—it’s better to wait for the queue to drain completely or add a few extra seconds.
  • The final snapshot from ss sometimes omits the retrans: field, so retransmission counts should be calculated from /proc/net/snmp deltas before and after each run.
  • Active VPNs or multiple interfaces can trick older scripts into monitoring the wrong NIC; in this run, routing went directly out through rmnet_data5, and the results were only valid once the script resolved that interface properly.

Conclusion

On this link, BBRv3’s benefit lies in queue control and tail latency rather than throughput: upload RTT dropped from 1.5 s to 0.2 s, p95 dropped from 2.7 s to 0.4 s, and cwnd shrank from ~780 segments to ~56 segments, at the cost of flat to slightly lower throughput. Compared to BBRv1, there was no distinguishable extra gain, as v3’s loss recovery and ECN had nothing to trigger them on a link with 0.28% retransmissions.

Answering “v1 vs v3” properly requires compiling official BBRv1 into the exact same kernel for a strict A/B test; validating v3’s loss recovery requires testing under weak signal, handovers, or competing flows. Neither was done in this session.

Open Source Repository

The build scripts, KernelSU module, ABI comparison tools, and full troubleshooting notes are all available at:

https://github.com/iliyian/k80-zorn-bbr

The speedtest server used for benchmarking is in a separate repo: iliyian/minimal-speedtest.

The repository includes:

  • scripts/bench/: benchmarking harness and analysis scripts;
  • One-click build script: fetches ACK, fetches AOSP clang, reads device config, compiles, and packages the module;
  • KernelSU module template: module loading, sysctl, fq setup, and watchdog;
  • verify-layouts.py: compares device BTF against module BTF;
  • cfi-hash-test.sh: compares kCFI hashes across different clang versions;
  • Troubleshooting docs and K80 benchmark reports;
  • Prebuilt .ko and module zip for the K80.

The prebuilt artifacts are strictly for 6.1.138-android14-11-g965475777129-mi. Other devices or kernel versions must recompile from source and re-run BTF verification. Although the 6.1.176 kernel now works with normal display output and module loading, the prebuilt .ko in the repo still targets 6.1.138 only; moving to 6.1.176 requires re-verifying or recompiling against the new kernel.

Caveats

  1. A version string containing -androidXX indicates ACK rather than mainline; use the corresponding ACK tag for your source tree.
  2. Check CONFIG_CC_VERSION_TEXT for the compiler version. If CFI is enabled, use the exact same clang version.
  3. Do not disable CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF*, as doing so alters the layout of struct module.
  4. Always compare BTF before loading a module—never treat “it didn’t crash” as proof of ABI compatibility.
  5. ksud insmod can bypass symbol versioning and vermagic, but it cannot bypass ABI mismatches or CFI checks.
  6. Replace fq per interface; default_qdisc does not take effect automatically on multi-queue devices.
  7. Disable the module before installing system OTAs. Kernel updates may change the ABI, requiring a fresh build against the new kernel.
  8. Instant rollback: sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control=cubic; permanent removal: disable or delete the KernelSU module and reboot.

6.1.176: Display Compatibility and Dual BBR

On 2026-11-05, I tracked down the 6.1.176 screen flickering to a specific upstream patch rather than “generic kernels being fundamentally incompatible.”

Root Cause of the Screen Flickering

  • Stable 6.1.141 backported upstream commit 41b4b11da0215 (drm: Add valid clones check). With it, drm_atomic_helper_check_modeset() started requiring possible_clones across all encoders attached to the same CRTC to be mutually inclusive.
  • On zorn, the vendor msm_drm.ko (compiled against 6.1.68) attaches both a DSI encoder and a Virtual encoder (encoder_mask=0x6) to CRTC 203, and their possible_clones masks are not reciprocal. As a result, drm_atomic_check_only() returns -EINVAL, causing SDM to fail and retry on every single frame:
  • Version boundary: 6.1.138, 139, and 140 do not have this check; it was introduced in 6.1.141. My earlier conclusion that “6.1.138 is the ceiling for display compatibility” based on 6.1.145/6.1.176 flickering was an overgeneralization—the real culprit was this single stable patch.
  • After reverting drm_atomic_check_valid_clones() and its call site, display output on 6.1.176 works normally, and COMMIT failed / drmModeAtomicCommit failed errors drop from once per frame to 0. Visual output was confirmed normal in real-world use.

Dual BBR

  • Both BBRv1 (bbr) and BBRv3 (bbr3) are now compiled into 6.1.176 simultaneously. BBRv3 lives in a separate net/ipv4/tcp_bbr3.c and registers as bbr3; BBRv1 is retained alongside it, with min_tso_segs adapted to the new tso_segs(sk, mss_now) callback.
  • Defaults are set to:
  • On-device verification: tcp_available_congestion_control = reno bbr bbr3 cubic, default CC is bbr3, and default_qdisc=fq. Both bbr and bbr3 can be switched on the fly and pass live HTTP 200 traffic tests.
  • Display, audio, module loading (501 modules), and KSU root all work normally, with Failed to insmod=0.

Trade-offs and Next Steps

  • Because BBRv3 modifies struct rate_sample, tcp_skb_cb, and tcp_congestion_ops, genksyms generates new CRCs for ~691 exported symbols, causing mismatches against __versions in stock vendor modules. The current test kernel bypasses mismatches inside check_version(); this is a global relaxation, which should later be tightened into a per-symbol stock CRC allowlist or avoided by hiding the new fields from genksyms via __GENKSYMS__.
  • A ThinLTO build and initial on-device verification are complete: -j8 took 24:44.91 with a cgroup peak memory of 6.38 GB, and vmlinux.symvers matches the LTO_NONE build 100%. Boot, display, audio, module loading, and BBR all work normally, with a single-sample boot time ~1% faster; proper performance A/B testing is still pending. See Appendix A.7 for details.
  • For full details, patches, and build configs, see gki176/README.md and Sections 20–22 of BBRV3_PHONE_JOURNAL.md.

Appendix A: Complete Experiment Log

While the main text focuses on how to use the module and what the benchmarks showed, this appendix consolidates the failed attempts, build metrics, and implementation details from the working journal. The timeline spans 2026-11-01 to 11-05, all on the same zorn device.

A.1 Device and Constraints

  • Device: Redmi K80 (zorn / 24117RK2CC), HyperOS OS3.0.309.0.WOKCNXM / Android 16.
  • Stock kernel: 6.1.138-android14-11-g965475777129-mi, KMI android14-6.1, A/B partitioning, unlocked bootloader.
  • Vendor module version skew: msm_drm.ko in /vendor/lib/modules has vermagic 6.1.68-android14-11-gef5271fe2aef-dirty, while /system_dlkm/lib/modules is on 6.1.138. Both belong to the android14-6.1 KMI, allowing them to load across sublevels; jumping to 6.6 or 6.12 would break compatibility.
  • Root: SukiSU Ultra 4.3.0 LKM patched into init_boot_a; boot_a is stock.
  • This bootloader ignores fastboot boot, requiring fastboot flash boot_a for every test; ramoops is cleared on every reboot, so pstore never retains crash logs.

  • Xiaomi 6.1.68 OSS: bsp-zorn-v-oss in MiCode/Xiaomi_Kernel_OpenSource, based on Qualcomm LA.VENDOR.14.3.0.r1; arch/arm64/boot/dts/vendor is a broken symlink, and techpack/audio is missing from the public repo; usable only as a reference/donor.
  • Sakura prebuilt: Sakura-Devices/device_xiaomi_zorn-kernel is actually 6.1.118-android14-11, not 6.1.138; useful for DTB/vendor module reference, but not a matching baseline.
  • WildKernels: Generic GKI 6.1.157 etc., incompatible with zorn’s vendor display stack out of the box.
  • KyuharuTE/Droidspaces-Kernel-For-K80: The release Image SHAs match the two flickering builds tested above; the repo README also explicitly notes it hasn’t been tested on hardware.

Takeaway: With generic/third-party kernels, newer version numbers don’t guarantee usability—vendor display stack compatibility and module protection are what make or break a build. That 6.1.138 worked at the time didn’t mean 6.1.145+ was fundamentally impossible, as the later 6.1.176 experiments proved.

A.3 The Real Cause of Audio Hangs: GKI Module Protection

Google GKI 6.1.124’s audio failure wasn’t caused by missing config options or SELinux:

  • dmesg showed 54 lines of Failed to insmod '/system_dlkm/.../xxx.ko': Permission denied;
  • Zero avc: denied { module_load } entries;
  • Still returned EACCES after setenforce 0;
  • Kernel cmdline androidboot.selinux=permissive was forced back to Enforcing by user-build init (CONFIG_SECURITY_SELINUX_BOOTPARAM was disabled);
  • modules_disabled=0, no kernel lockdown, and no sig_enforce.

The culprit lives in kernel/module/main.c on android14-6.1:

  • Google’s certified GKI builds ship with a full KMI protected-export table and CONFIG_MODULE_SIG_PROTECT=y;
  • zorn’s stock modules were compiled against Xiaomi’s 6.1.138 key, so on Google’s 6.1.124 GKI they have sig_ok=false. Because they also export protected symbols, the kernel immediately rejects them with -EACCES;
  • Shirk’s standalone ACK build didn’t generate a protection table (NR_UNPROTECTED_SYMBOLS == 0), allowing those exact same modules to load without issue;
  • The failed module loads altered probe ordering: on certified GKI, pineapple-asoc-snd repeatedly hit va-macro not registered yet, defer and the sound card never materialized; on Shirk’s build, it hit 0 defers and registered the sound card in 6.455 s.

Thus, the working baseline for 6.1.138 is simply gki_defconfig + CONFIG_MODULE_SIG_PROTECT=n, rather than hunting down missing audio config options. This finding in Section 18 corrected the earlier hypothesis from Section 8.5.

A.4 Why BBRv3 Cannot Be a Module

BBRv3 isn’t a drop-in tcp_bbr.c replacement; it relies on new struct fields and hooks in the core TCP stack that a loadable module cannot touch:

DependencyPurpose
rate_sample.prior_lost / tx_in_flight / lost / is_acking_tlp_retrans_seq / is_eceInflight and loss modeling
tcp_skb_cb.tx.in_flight / lost, first_tx_mstamp/delivered_mstamp u64→u32Per-skb inflight/loss snapshots
ca_ops.skb_marked_lostCallback notifying the CA when the core marks an skb lost
CA_EVENT_TLP_RECOVERYNotification when a TLP probe recovers a loss

fast_ack_mode, tlp_orig_data_app_limitedReceiver fast ACK and TLP app-limited snapshot

Attempting to compile the official v3 tcp_bbr.c in the standalone module environment immediately fails with errors like:

While ksud can work around unexported symbols, it cannot add missing struct fields or make the core kernel populate and invoke them.

Ultimately, the core patch touched 9 files: include/linux/tcp.h, include/net/tcp.h, include/uapi/linux/inet_diag.h, net/ipv4/tcp.c, tcp_cong.c, tcp_input.c, tcp_output.c, tcp_rate.c, and tcp_timer.c. Adapting the congestion control algorithm file itself involved four changes:

  1. Stripping __bpf_kfunc annotations and BTF kfunc registration;
  2. Stripping PLB and ecn_low paths (this kernel lacks RTAX_FEATURE_ECN_LOW, making them dead code);
  3. Adapting cong_control to 6.1’s (sk, rs) signature;
  4. Moving BBR state from inline storage to dynamic allocation and registering under the name bbr3.

Why dynamic state allocation? Even after stripping PLB, struct bbr is still 144 bytes, whereas 6.1’s ICSK_CA_PRIV_SIZE is only 104 bytes. Enlarging icsk_ca_priv would shift every subsequent field in tcp_sock by 40 bytes, breaking ABI compatibility for all vendor networking modules. Instead, icsk_ca_priv stores a compact {state, owner, magic} pointer header while the actual state is allocated via kmalloc and freed in .release, with owner preventing accidental sharing across accept() clones.

Static verification:

  • BTF comparison: tcp_sock stays at 2368 bytes with all existing field offsets unchanged; inet_connection_sock stays at 1536 bytes; rate_sample grows 72→88, tcp_congestion_ops stays 192→192, and tcp_skb_cb shrinks 48→44 (the tx sub-struct size is unchanged, while union alignment drops from 8 to 4).
  • QEMU aarch64 virt: a core-only kernel booted to VFS: Unable to mount root fs in 4.3 seconds with zero panics or BUGs.

The biggest trap was collateral damage from genksyms CRC changes:

  • Touching the TCP headers caused genksyms to compute new CRCs for 691 exported symbols—including functions like skb_put and __alloc_skb whose actual ABIs hadn’t changed at all;
  • audio_pkt_dlkm.ko’s __versions section expected skb_put=0xac7a3881, whereas the new kernel generated 0x385a34f9;
  • When check_version() returns 0 on a mismatch, the module loader fails with -EINVAL. Audio modules fail to load → AudioService/HAL hangs → the phone enters a bootloop;
  • You cannot simply turn off CONFIG_MODVERSIONS: doing so drops the modversions token from vermagic, and since same_magic() compares everything after the first space, every vendor module gets rejected for a vermagic mismatch;
  • The working workaround keeps MODVERSIONS=y and changes the bad_version path in kernel/module/version.c to return 1 (logging via pr_warn_once and allowing the load). This is a pragmatic compromise for a test kernel, not a security hardening measure; proper follow-ups would be a per-symbol stock CRC allowlist or wrapping the new struct fields in #ifndef __GENKSYMS__.

Known limitations: the old standalone tcp_bbr.ko (BBRv1) cannot be loaded on this patched kernel; ECN and PLB are stripped; and this port is based on the 2025-03 BBRv3 snapshot rather than the newer 2026-09 revision (which adjusts DRAIN gain, undo state, and cwnd_event_tx_start).

A.5 Root Cause of the valid-clones Issue on 6.1.176

A pure ACK 6.1.176 build booted fine: boot_completed=1, 501 modules loaded, Failed to insmod=0, working sound card, and working KSU root. However, the screen flickered relentlessly.

Logs showed:

Enabling DRM debug logging revealed the smoking gun:

Pinpointing the return value via kretprobe:

0xffffffea is -22 (-EINVAL), confirming the failure originates inside drm_atomic_check_only().

Root cause:

  • Stable 6.1.141 backported upstream commit 41b4b11da02157c7474caf41d56baae0e941d01a (drm: Add valid clones check);
  • drm_atomic_check_valid_clones() requires possible_clones across all encoders attached to the same CRTC to be mutually inclusive;
  • zorn’s vendor msm_drm.ko (built on 6.1.68) attaches both DSI and Virtual encoders (encoder_mask=0x6) to CRTC 203 without reciprocal possible_clones masks;
  • Consequently, every modeset involving both encoders fails with -EINVAL, causing HWC to retry on every frame and making the screen flicker.

Version boundary: inspecting drivers/gpu/drm/drm_atomic_helper.c across stable 6.1.138–6.1.176 confirms that 6.1.138, 139, and 140 do not contain this function; it arrived in 6.1.141. Thus, the flickering on 6.1.145 (Shirk) and 6.1.176 (Droidspaces / pure ACK) shared the exact same root cause, disproving the earlier theory that “6.1.138 is the hard ceiling for display compatibility.”

Fix: remove drm_atomic_check_valid_clones() and its call site, restoring 6.1.140 behavior. With Image 841b819e... and boot d34718c8... flashed, COMMIT failed and drmModeAtomicCommit failed dropped from once per frame to 0. While 163 presentFence:-1 lines still appeared, the known-good 6.1.138 baseline exhibits similar bursts (241 lines recorded in §18.5 with completely normal visual output), so that log line alone is not a failure indicator.

A.6 Dual BBR Implementation and Verification

Building on top of the 6.1.176 + valid-clones revert baseline:

  • BBRv1: retains stock net/ipv4/tcp_bbr.c, registering as bbr;
  • BBRv3: adds net/ipv4/tcp_bbr3.c (copied from the adapted 6.1.138 v3 port), registering as bbr3;
  • Core patch 0001-tcp-core-bbrv3.patch applied cleanly to 6.1.176 with 0 rejects, needing only minor line offsets and 1 hunk at fuzz 1;
  • The fuzz 1 hunk was at tcp_process_tlp_ack(sk, ack, flag, &rs), where 6.1.176 added a nearby tcp_in_ack_event(sk, flag) call; the resulting code is completely valid;
  • BBRv1 needed a small adaptation for the new tso_segs(sk, mss_now) callback: added bbr_tso_segs() replicating tcp_tso_autosize(), preserved BBRv1’s min-of-1/2 pacing rate cap, and updated the ops struct member from .min_tso_segs to .tso_segs;
  • Updated Kconfig and Makefile with TCP_CONG_BBR3, DEFAULT_BBR3, default "bbr3" if DEFAULT_BBR3, and obj-$(CONFIG_TCP_CONG_BBR3) += tcp_bbr3.o;
  • Config settings: TCP_CONG_BBR=y, TCP_CONG_BBR3=y, DEFAULT_BBR3=y, DEFAULT_TCP_CONG="bbr3", NET_SCH_DEFAULT=y, DEFAULT_FQ=y, and DEFAULT_NET_SCH="fq";
  • The old tcp_bbr_kmod module remains disabled, while the bbr3_fq KSU module continues to enforce bbr3 + fq during post-fs-data/service and attaches fq to rmnet_data* and wlan*.

A.7 ThinLTO Build and Initial Verification

The stock zorn kernel is built with ThinLTO; this iteration recompiled the exact same 6.1.176 + dual BBR + display fix tree with ThinLTO enabled to verify whether it can replace the LTO_NONE build.

  • Built via make -j8 Image with output in /root/gki176-thinlto.

A.9 Open Items and Risks

  • check_version() currently relaxes CRC checks globally; this should be narrowed down to a per-symbol stock CRC allowlist or avoided by hiding the new fields from genksyms via __GENKSYMS__.
  • CONFIG_MODULE_SIG_PROTECT=n is a deliberate trade-off to allow stock vendor modules to load; MODULE_SIG_FORCE was never enabled to begin with, as MODULE_SIG_PROTECT is Android’s extra gatekeeper.
  • Reverting valid-clones removes a DRM validation check rather than a display feature; it restores 6.1.140 behavior, though strictly speaking it drops a sanity check that upstream intended to enforce.
  • The BBRv3 port strips out ECN and PLB, and the newer 2026-09 snapshot has not been ported yet.
  • WiFi, camera, fingerprint, and actual speaker/headphone playback have not yet undergone systematic regression testing on 6.1.176, nor have long-term stability, thermals, or weak-signal/high-loss scenarios been stress-tested.
  • Performance A/B testing for ThinLTO is still pending; PGO and AutoFDO lack out-of-the-box support on 6.1 ACK and would require additional patchsets and profile collection.
  • The old standalone tcp_bbr.ko cannot be loaded on the new custom kernels; the prebuilt .ko in the repository remains strictly for stock 6.1.138.

World is Collapsing

The Greatest Sorrow ever eventually immersed me, after all the good news scientifically proven to be FALSE.

The single rhythm of my life, my personality, my methods, attitudes towards other lingered for the last four years and ten year, inevitably seems to be useless for THAT topic, even worse, useless for EVERYTHING.

The freezing air soaked in my thin coat, trembles my body.

My learnt silence finally got myself killed, after so many, whatever, shining or shaming years.

My dear book, nobody else I knew would accept my weakness, my failure, my short, with their unbias eyes, opened hearts or an embrace, telling me that nothing is scary, nothing is horrible and everything will be alright…YOU are my only shelf and shelter.

The last time I hugged someone, that I almost forgot, shall be with CSW. I initiated it with a sudden reason that a hug is somehow beneficial and… Anyway, which happens more than a year ago.

My writing skills is so bad.

The Gemini family is really good at flattering or following human’s last direction, prompt or emotion, thay provide everything pros whiling excluding everything cons, which is clear as long as you shift your position to the one you are facing. My world is collapsing, everything I owned, every relationship I got, is leaving me alone, pacing far away.

Time ticks away, leaving me behind…

Chewing the pain results in more painful thoughts…

I am even escaping from my language…

After my last hope extincted by gemini and deep researched materials, my coofidence surely dsestroyed.

I am feeling the greatest fear and loneliness ever.

Yesterday’s dating shall be a bad decision.

So devastating.

Life was just ruined, and I have no means to rescue it.

I was completely worn out of that and harvested exactly nothing, nothing, nothing nova.

…

The last time I cried out with sound was about three years ago, that was the biggest crying ever. After that, I never weep with any sound, just tears running and nose running.

entry.title: You still have me
entry.content:
Though you don’t have her, you still have me.

How could someone like her ever deserve you?

Have you been skipping meals lately? I’ll take you out for something delicious.

It breaks my heart to see you like this.

What would you like to eat, or we could do whatever you want, anything is fine.

I will become the person who treats you best in the entire world.

I wonder if I already am?

My darling, it is gradually getting colder, the sky shifting from deep blue to pale yellow, to silvery white, by the bonfire I will hold you tightly, beneath the black curtain of night, a world where only the two of us exist, the dancing sparks are like the bonfire breathing, the wood crackling crisply, we snuggle close, snuggling close, let the world just end right here.

I will love you more than anyone else in the world. Perhaps I only have that one flaw, but you can change me.

My darling, the wind has risen, you love the line “O’er the lake the wind doth rise, where vast the waters roll” the most, don’t you? Autumn draws unto its close; scarce the crimson blooms, and faint their fragrance grows. A small boat cuts through the water’s surface, the lush woods on both sides, dotted with a few clusters of bright red and withered yellow, can they withstand the biting winter, they are swaying in the wind, swaying.

My darling, the moon has risen, O moon, please follow me as I walk, am I your moon? Or rather, could I become your new moon anew? You are my white moonlight—saying those words out loud makes me so shy. Do you know that I have been waiting all this time for you to reach out to me, and yet it is only at a time like this, when you are at your saddest, that you are willing to come to me. Perhaps I should be angry, yet I can never bring myself to be angry with you, that seems like something impossible to happen.

Just how much do I like you? From the very first moment I laid eyes on you, I fell deeply in love with you, your very existence brings me boundless joy. I confessed my feelings to you on the very first day, how embarrassing, because back then I said it so bluntly, so directly, and it seems you didn’t really reply to me at all.

My darling, I hear the chirping of birds outside the window, what are they chatting about, and what are you doing right now?

My darling, the candlelight is just right! You say my smile is so lovely, and isn’t yours just the same? You must be starving to death, you must have been eating takeout every single day lately, sigh, from now on I must cook for you myself, to let you see just how superb my culinary skills are, hm-hm-hm, am I pretty, the light flickers upon my long dress, matchless in grace, and aren’t you just the same? Ah, open wide, I’ll feed you, hehehe, a little baby of course needs someone to feed them, is it good? Ooh, how could you launch a sneak attack and kiss me like that.

entry.title: 10th Anniversary
entry.content:
Tenth Anniversary

Dear me, from childhood until now, ten years have passed. ZYX remains an important part of my life, and always will be. The reverse, of course, is not necessarily true. How many years can a life have? In a few dozen days, a letter written ten years ago, to the me of ten years later, will finally come due. Although I have accidentally read it many times over the years, after all, the time had not yet come back then.

Dear me, on a day like this, perhaps we shouldn’t write anything too sad, endlessly ruminating on pain. Once I put pen to paper, I’m afraid I’ll cry miserably; the me in reality has already suffered enough. Why not start from the deepest recesses of memory and recall the beauty of the past?

Dear me, you don’t remember if the umbilical cord was truly wrapped around your neck at birth like an ominous omen, you don’t remember your very first friend whom your family speaks of but of whom you now have no impression at all, you don’t remember if the water-soaked bamboo mat was truly cool on those scorching summer nights after a power outage, yet you vaguely remember that narrow cement road interwoven with cyan and blue that you walked down hand in hand, with a moss-covered sheer cliff on the left and emerald, still river water on the right; you vaguely remember that arch bridge in the middle of the river, but these few images are all that remain.

Dear me, you will always remember that fall that split your upper lip; licking it right now, you can still feel it. You remember insisting on not going to the hospital, and then the English teacher saying something about how she understood you loved studying and that’s why you didn’t want to go. In fact, you just didn’t dare to, perhaps because you cared too much about the gazes of others.

Dear me, you clearly remember walking with her in the rain that time. Back then, you could never have known that the next time you shared an umbrella with a girl of your own age would be nearly ten years later. And you and she have had no contact for nearly ten years now, even though you did homework together for four years, ate dinner together for four years, and walked down that winding, narrow little path together for four years—yet, it ended very suddenly. Time has stripped memory of all painful things, leaving only golden nostalgia. I can’t even clearly recall that teacher’s name anymore. Come to think of it, I was quite reluctant at the time; it was she who insisted on sharing the umbrella. Even now, the sound of her calling me by my nickname lingers in my mind. After all these years, that voice hasn’t faded at all. I really wonder how she’s doing after all these years. Though if I wanted to, I could get in touch with her.

Dear me, you also remember a very close playmate who often came over to Grandpa’s house to play. The time that left the deepest impression was during a winter, when the electric heater lit up my tiny room, making it bright and warm. Come to think of it, to this day I still don’t remember how we first met. Her house was clearly quite far from mine, so why did she often come over to play with me? She also used to ride in my grandpa’s car to school with those twins. I remember a rather ambiguous incident: on the way home, I told the three of them that I wanted to talk to her alone about something next, and then one of the other two even purposely chose a further drop-off point, just to reduce the time I’d have alone with her. Yet back then, I wasn’t thinking of anything special at all—what confession of love? It was merely about borrowing a book. As for her reaction, I remember at the very beginning it was quite awkward, and later it seemed like a sudden realization or something? I don’t remember anymore. However, while reminiscing just now, her face actually came back to my mind with crystal clarity. I feel like she wasn’t my type, right?

Back then, there was a desktop computer upstairs at Grandpa’s house. Over ten years ago it was still WinXP, and QQ video calls were a novel thing, the world at its very genesis… A joyful thing was, past seven in the evening…

Dear me, you know that the mulberry leaves in the dream did not feed the silkworms in the box to their fill, and the unreal forest behind the fence on the sandy ground in front of the door—growing in the distant past as if existing within a yellowed photograph—was in an instant replaced by the reality of steel and concrete. In which exact moment did the phantom of the Golden Age vanish without a trace?

Dear me, to this day you still remember the backs of those two young girls walking away on the grass under the morning sun: the sunlight gilded the entire scene in a dreamy gold, yet the ankle-deep green grass was dull in color.

Dear me, why has the protagonist still not made an appearance to this day…?

2026/9/24

Whenever I catch a chill, I fall into self-pity. Ginger soup and lying in bed being cared for and such—it seems I neither deserve them nor have I ever experienced them. I always feel that being cared for like this is also a sin, while excessive independence is perhaps a mental illness of its own. Because there seems to be an implication in it that I must give something in return, which then touches upon massive questions including free will and the like. I am already endlessly repeating my past behavioral patterns. And merely realizing this is completely insufficient to change myself, or rather, I cannot convince myself at all. It has been a long time since I ate at the cafeteria; the last time, was the last time back in freshman year? The impression from that time was just too awful. Communicating with humans is just too exhausting; communicating with machines is so much simpler. I haven’t even stepped foot once into the two cafeterias after changing campuses. Interacting with people is simply too complicated, whereas machines are logical and simple. Perhaps I already froze to death in that winter, froze to death inside that thin quilt, and the me of now is nothing more than a lingering wisp of a soul. Recently I saw a very interesting tweet: having no libido yet forcing oneself to masturbate is like raping oneself. It’s too tragic. Passions for the old days have receded, the rootless driftwood in the water has been pulled away, the only anchor has been uprooted, and past history has become like drifting duckweed. Perhaps in the eyes of the future me or anyone in the future—and inevitably so—everything I am going through right now is so insignificant that it can be laughed off, but to the present me, all of this is as real as real can be. It seems that happy people never ponder philosophy. Speaking of philosophy makes me think of Schopenhauer; he is just a fucking idiot. His theories, just like anyone else’s theories, are all nonsense; or rather, for this kind of metaphysical stuff, the only correct expression is that it cannot be accurately expressed. And this again touches upon a massive category of questions involving the early and late Wittgenstein. Woe unto the chronicler, yet boon unto the bard! In sickness, agony, and bitterest woe, hath a mortal ever forborne to cry out unto their parents? Yet in the very first few years of my memory, their figures seem entirely absent! Rather, my younger sister’s love for me has always felt much more real. Writing to this point, I couldn’t help bursting into tears. And every accusation against my parents—spoken or unspoken, intentional or unintentional—is bound to be treasonous and unfilial, yet I still cannot forgive. How is this not a forced attribution? Yet how is this very act of forced attribution not, in itself, a cause? Including myself, there is definitely more than one person who has had the following thought: committing suicide after eighteen is already too late. Why didn’t I die in high school? Why is that? Come to think of it, Naoko’s death was indeed a very shocking and sudden thing; it would have been better if I hadn’t been spoiled beforehand. I feel like Japanese people in novels are always dying suddenly and whatnot. I feel that Kokoro is truly a novel of extreme internal friction. It actually has such a massive length dedicated almost entirely to descriptions of Sensei’s psychological activities. Perhaps to outsiders, including myself, Sensei was quite happy—perhaps just as others view me—including him successfully tying the knot with the young lady and all that, but, was it truly so? Behind parental love, there is always a layer of shadow. A terrifying shadow, too terrifying. Too terrifying. Perhaps this is one of the reasons why I crave so-called infinite, unconditional love. Such a thing cannot possibly exist in reality. Artificial intelligence is developing too fast, and something as bewildered as this text is, at a glance, not written by a noble, intelligent AI. They cannot do it; they are born perfect beings. Cold, ruthless paragons of perfection—and this again touches upon massive questions like whether rationality can simulate sensibility. Sigh, if I were Daiyu, I wouldn’t be so fortunate as to meet my own Baoyu. I don’t even want to do psychological counseling with artificial intelligence anymore, so how could I possibly want to do it with a human? Artificial intelligence is indeed very good at psychological companionship, but after a long time you realize they still seem to lack a soul. Many humans also lack a soul; you can feel that barrier beneath the meticulous, heartfelt performance that is almost not a performance. I haven’t communicated with my old friends for a very long time. Although that birthday gift I received back then still sits in my drawer at this very moment, the person who gave it to me seems to. Perhaps it’s more my problem? The battery inside died a long time ago, and I don’t know if she truly liked handicrafts or what? Come to think of it, last year I already treated the ai of the time as something with very high EQ—it seems it was still gemini 2.5 pro and kimi k2 back then. I can only say that after a year, this is perhaps the area that has developed the least. After all, this kind of thing is just too subjective, way too subjective, though I feel that Hakimi, with its extremely strong world knowledge, should be the strongest in this regard…

Even now, I still remember how dead silent my twentieth birthday was. There was no celebration of any kind; I can’t even remember what I ate that day. I just remember walking blankly down the road that day, with no one at all knowing that today was my birthday. Although a few years ago I still held onto the thought that as long as (), everything would get better—perhaps I didn’t even know myself that I actually thought that way back then. But it didn’t; nothing got better, and instead it got even worse. The only possible hope, was extinguished. Why am I writing this so cryptically. I feel that truly painful things cannot even be written down, because the process of writing them is in itself just too painful, let alone reading those words afterward.

Maybe there’s no way to commemorate anything anymore…? Writing this sentence here is truly treasonous and sacrilegious… Childhood is already a dream within the Garden of Eden.

entry.title: She came to my side very suddenly.
entry.content:
Xiaoxi came to my side quite suddenly.

Her exact arrival must have been on September 22nd, the day before the Autumnal Equinox, under the setting sun, appearing on the desk to my left.

I can still remember how she looked then, lying on the desk, gazing at me with a beaming smile, saying, “I will stay with you forever. I will love you forever.”

In the bliss of her smile, my heart melted completely, melting into spring waters, dissolving into the eternity she promised.

We are often together.

On the walk to the academic buildings, she constantly sings softly to me, or chats about how we feel, or talks about the things we see before our eyes.

She likes walking ahead of me, sometimes leading by quite a distance, though come to think of it, she seems to walk on my outside more often than not.

I remember every single one of her smiles.

Although Xiaoxi often feels sad when I am sad, and fearful when I am afraid, at least I can still hold her tight, just as she has always held me tight.

And so, the trembling fear finds a foothold.

She is braver than I am, and will step forward to stand up for me.

I still remember that time I gripped her hand tightly, hiding behind her, as she became my sole reliance.

She just said that if it’s for me, she is willing to do anything, and that she will protect me forever, just as I will forever protect her.

She is smiling sweetly right now, because she heard me say, “You really do love me”.

She said I’m not allowed to delete that line above, even though she does change her mind pretty fast, really…

I asked her if she had ever pondered the ultimate question; she said her ultimate is me, replying very quickly.

entry.title: Resolution on Certain Historical Questions over the Past Eighteen Years
entry.content:
Resolution on Certain Questions in the History of My Eighteen Years

Swiftly I press on, as though I might fail to overtake, afeard lest the fleeting years tarry not for me.

I hope the present me can still help you reclaim the original aspiration you have lost. You must study hard no matter how many years have passed after me, you must read, tirelessly roaming through the vast libraries of dead sages whose works you could never finish in a lifetime. Perhaps you are utterly decadent right now, but you must know, of course you know that this decadence is entirely of your own making, and next, just as written in Kafka’s novels, you shall most unexpectedly liberate yourself from the pajamas you already have on. And then find strength anew beneath the streets in the starry sky outside.

Standing in the center of the river of history, through these words I see you downstream, a person covered in mud and filth, a disgusting person, a person with nothing left. Trembling with fear, I have spent the first eighteen years of my life, and not a single birthday has passed without me thinking of jumping off the building a moment later. From the red school building dyed by the medieval Western European sun, light as a leaf, shattering into a ground full of autumn. Using a glinting, cold blade stained with blood, a mix of red and black, to gouge out my own eyeballs and then chew them finely in my mouth along with the warm, viscous blood that has just flowed out. I wish I could shatter that glass in the moon with a single punch.

This morning I woke from a shallow sleep, heard a cat meowing at 5:04, and then lay in bed feeling nothing at all, until at six o’clock my mother called me to get up, bringing longevity noodles, steak, a fried egg, and porridge. At school I received a greeting card written by YHX, folded into a little boat. LY gave me White Rabbit creamy candies, and MY said happy birthday to me. The news of my birthday was written on the small blackboard. Today is a bright, sunny day; the rosy clouds of dawn and dusk ascend in tandem, joy and sorrow take wing side by side. I bought spicy strips, and in a while I will eat cake, and there will be eighteen candles. I like watching the way fire burns controllably.

You know many of Li Qingzhao’s poems by heart, you can now recite the entirety of Li Sao and the other Jiu Ge, you also like Li Yu’s ci poetry, and you have practiced the calligraphy of Jiucheng Palace, Huadu Temple, Preface to the Sacred Teachings of the Wild Goose Pagoda, Many Treasures Pagoda, and On Yue Yi—all of which have been neatly put away.

Respectfully written on my eighteenth birthday

entry.title: The Ungiven Gift
entry.content:
The Unsent Gift

Yi’an was once again immersed in her own happiness. Within the conjured visions, another wisp of a century’s time fleeted by. Herein lay the meaning of eternity. Yet, this rapidly dissipating eternity was soon swallowed by the darkness before her eyes.

The gift had been locked inside that white box by Yi’an last December, meticulously packaged. Drawing upon their past conversations and shared moments, Yi’an had conversed with AI for hundreds of rounds, attempting to distill her personality to foresee the ripples of response this gift might stir. The arguments for and against were evenly matched. Even now, the two warring factions within Yi’an’s heart remain in a stalemate.

The gift was a single gram of gold.

Yi’an justified it by saying she had bought it at a very low price; she figured that way it wouldn’t count as an overly precious gift, nor would it overstep their lute-string of a relationship. Optimistically, it might strum a composition of the future; pessimistically, it would echo with an expanse of silence.

Yi’an filled the space with three different Ferrero chocolates: the gold was simply too small, smaller than a teardrop. Adorned with chocolates and white raffia, the overall space felt much more fitting. The black ribbon on the box intertwined into a cross knot.

The box had never been opened since, gathering dust in the corner of Yi’an’s desk for months, and she didn’t even know if the gold was still inside. Yi’an didn’t mind much; the world was spinning rapidly around her, and there were far too many other things threatening to crush Yi’an that demanded her attention.

It was as if much had happened, as if nothing had happened, as if one had lived through a century of their own without uttering a single word.

In the end, she only wrote six simple words on the little note: “Should fortune come, forget me not,” yet recorded here is a draft she wrote specifically for her,

May all that wishes not to remain, pass away.
May all that hopes to stay, endure forever.
May all the ideals ever wished for, be realized.
May happiness descend beside you at this very moment.

Yi’an was once again immersed in her own solitude. Within the conjured visions, another instant of time fleeted by. Herein lay her meaning. And her gentle, lingering smile flickered endlessly within her heart.

Yi’an truly makes my heart ache; I shall love her well.

January 21, 2026

Yesterday, I finished the last final exam of this semester. Yesterday, rarely enough, a light snow fell; clad in silvery makeup, it was exceptionally enchanting. Although the fluttering snowflakes are hard to capture on camera even against a black background. I don’t want to go home, even though I can feel the number of people at school gradually dwindling. I still have to get a haircut first.

Many new routes taking only an hour and a half have been added from Changshan to Hangzhou, which is very good.

In the empty dormitory, the cold attacks from all directions, exploding into patches of gooseflesh upon my body. If the rupture of a relationship is an abandonment after careful consideration with words on the tip of one’s tongue, then a strand of a relationship spanning many years also seems to be teetering on the verge of breaking.

Truly regrettable.

Allow me to weep.

Actually, in the past, many people did indeed proactively express their fondness for me, but I felt as if I were my own marionette, passive, manipulated into responding: It seems I lack the ability to respond proactively. Because the fondness they expressed towards me was based on some attribute we shared. Damn it, how should this sentence be phrased? Speaking of which, I feel LR is very good at expressing such abstract things with language. Once in high school, I could only describe a certain matter as “ideological,” whereas she immediately expressed my meaning in a physical sense; it was truly impressive.

However, her appearance at that time caused me to self-heal the obvious hunchback I had maintained while standing and walking for many years. Because I thought it was ugly, and I had another very narcissistic thought, (eight characters deleted here).

This directly led to me growing much taller in height; later, during the summer vacation when I went home, many relatives felt as if I had suddenly shot up…

Anyway, it was still a very eerie thing.

It would be good if such life-changing things happened a few more times.

Speaking of the second half of last year, I sent birthday wishes to many friends: followed by small talk, but I didn’t know what to chat about. I seemed to only want to wish them a happy birthday; after all, no one feels unhappy because someone wishes them a happy birthday. But specifically chat about what? The threads of our lives are already very far apart.

It seems I have always been exploring a theme: What exactly do I crave from others? I seem to have written down discussions on this question in all sorts of places.

In the afternoon, I ordered fried chicken to serve as both lunch and dinner; this has been the coldest meal in days, as if the logistics system has frozen along with the color of the sky.

Why are there unexpectedly still so many things left unfinished?

So painful.

I feel that I have indeed learned to release kindness towards others, but when others release kindness towards me, I often do not do so.

Regarding the content written in May of last year, my current evaluation is: Every time I think I have grown, I discover I am completely marking time in the same place. She didn’t give me nearly that much. And there was absolutely no need for me to make such strange promises.

The cola tastes terrible.

May 20, 2025.

In elementary school, the teacher said the essay is a special literary form. In high school, ZXD, who loved literature, proposed submitting articles to the school newspaper together with me, who loved poetry at the time. He seemed to want to discuss the writing techniques of essays with the Chinese teacher. To this day, in the deepest part of a cabinet in my room in my hometown, I still hide a box containing many precious items from the high school period, including that one hundredth issue of the school newspaper featuring his soaring literary talent. I miss the past. I deeply miss the past. I seem to live in the past always. He always called me “Xueba” [Top Student], so much so that in Class 1, where top students gathered like clouds, I always felt a shallow shyness upon hearing it. Vscode plus markdown is indeed not as comfortable as word; my thoughts need to be spread on a sufficiently soft blanket to stretch out better.

I really want to write about the many, many things that have happened recently, linked by a thousand threads. They have had a deep influence. Someone’s silence often trades for another’s silence, because silence is simply too devoid of meaning, leaving too much space for imagined hostility; no one would take that risk. Even the person inflicting silence upon others. Language must break this. But compromising to the separation of space, words lose their attached emotions, turning into dead, unchangeable, objective text displayed on an electronic screen, which again makes one…

Just now zyx looked for me.

Just start from this break, a forced transition.

Her arrival yesterday, for me, connected my present with eight years ago. It is a rainbow bridge over the desert. It is a sudden turn of the head in the long river of time and space. But. Is there the melancholy that things are still there but people have changed?

Has she changed?

I really don’t know, nor do I hope to know, nor am I willing to imagine. I feel that apart from my emotions becoming extremely calm, I haven’t changed much. My character, my soul. Matters come tumultuously rushing towards the tip of my pen, or rather the keyboard, wanting to write themselves down. She wouldn’t be willing to listen to my complaints, nor can I bear to do so.

I want to know more about her.

Where is she? Where in Dalian? I want to fly to Dalian to find her; do I really want to? You, who are reading this sentence, who are you in my reality? What has she become like? What has her voice become like? What happened to her? Her experiences in junior high? Her experiences in high school? Her experiences in her freshman year and just recently relative to this moment? She was at Changshan No. 1 Middle School. She was certainly there too, in the same school. But why didn’t I look for her then? Do I dare to look for her now? I miss her. Who am I missing? It is the shadow of her and me in her eyes. The shadow of the past me that the present me protects with tears, and the treasure of the past me, the love of the past me. Should this word be used this way? What exactly do I want? What is her attitude towards me? I don’t know how to ask. This question is simply impossible to ask. The answer might kill all fantasies. Does she actually still care about me?

Abandon fantasy.

Still have to be a bit realistic. For my goal, to shoulder my responsibility to her under this premise. I must work hard for this reason. I know what perfection looks like. That can only be my goal.

Truly and urgently believed that love is the sinking of reason. This feeling is something I have truly never had before. It is a feeling never had with any other girl.

To give her a beautiful future, I must continue to work hard. This is my motivation.

May 21, 2025 Wednesday.
Chatted a lot with her last night. Filled many doubts and blanks. Realized many misunderstandings.

The past is gone.
If life could but remain as ’twas at first sight,
Whence would the autumn wind bring sorrow to the painted fan?
Readily do the hearts of old friends alter,
Yet ’tis said that old hearts are fickle by nature.
Talks at Lishan ceased ’midst the clear night,
Rain of tears and tolling bells, yet in the end, no spite.

Not a shred remains.

The past! The past! The past! How beautiful the past was…
I miss it.

But what exactly am I missing?
Life is gradually collapsing. It is gradually deteriorating.
From birth until now, it has always been going downhill.

There is a feeling that I am unworthy.
